intro.text: This entry describes orofaciodigital syndrome XX (OFD20), a ciliopathy in the orofaciodigital syndrome group. I cannot confidently recall the causative gene or the primary reports that defined this numbered subtype, so no gene is named here.

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndrome XX (OFD20) is a ciliopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Affected individuals presented a novel form of OFDS (OFDS-RAB34) accompanied by cardiac, cerebral, skeletal and anorectal defects.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a novel ciliary OFDS caused by RAB34 but never uses the designation OFD20/orofaciodigital syndrome XX.

checks.claim: Orofaciodigital syndrome XX (OFD20) belongs to the orofaciodigital syndrome group.
checks.evidence_quote: Affected individuals presented a novel form of OFDS (OFDS-RAB34) accompanied by cardiac, cerebral, skeletal and anorectal defects.
checks.explanation: The abstract places the novel disorder within OFDS, but the OFD20 numbering does not appear in it.

paragraphs.text: The orofaciodigital syndromes are a clinically and genetically heterogeneous group of ciliopathies. They are defined by abnormalities of the oral cavity (such as lobulated or hamartomatous tongue, oral frenulae, and cleft lip and/or palate), the face, and the digits (such as polydactyly, syndactyly, and brachydactyly). Some patients also have brain malformations and involvement of other organs. OFD20 is one of the numbered subtypes. I do not remember its specific defining reports well enough to describe them.

checks.claim: The orofaciodigital syndromes are a clinically heterogeneous group of disorders.
checks.evidence_quote: Oral-facial-digital syndromes (OFDS) are a group of clinically and genetically heterogeneous disorders

checks.claim: The orofaciodigital syndromes are a genetically heterogeneous group of disorders.
checks.evidence_quote: Oral-facial-digital syndromes (OFDS) are a group of clinically and genetically heterogeneous disorders
Pathogenic variants in over 20 genes encoding ciliary proteins have been found to cause OFDS through deleterious structural or functional impacts on primary cilia.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not use the word ciliopathy, but it follows directly from causation by defects of the primary cilium.

checks.evidence_quote: characterized by defects in the development of the face and oral cavity along with digit anomalies
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions oral cavity defects but gives no examples (tongue hamartomas, frenulae, cleft lip/palate).

checks.evidence_quote: characterized by defects in the development of the face and oral cavity along with digit anomalies
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions digit anomalies but not the specific examples (polydactyly, syndactyly, brachydactyly).

checks.claim: Some patients with orofaciodigital syndrome have brain malformations.
checks.evidence_quote: Affected individuals presented a novel form of OFDS (OFDS-RAB34) accompanied by cardiac, cerebral, skeletal and anorectal defects.
checks.explanation: Cerebral defects are reported only for the RAB34 patients, not for OFDS patients in general.

checks.evidence_quote: Affected individuals presented a novel form of OFDS (OFDS-RAB34) accompanied by cardiac, cerebral, skeletal and anorectal defects.
checks.explanation: Other-organ involvement is reported only for the RAB34 patients, not for OFDS in general.

checks.claim: OFD20 is one of the numbered subtypes of orofaciodigital syndrome.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention numbered OFD subtypes or the OFD20 designation.

paragraphs.text: Orofaciodigital syndrome is genetically heterogeneous. Most numbered subtypes are caused by mutations in genes that encode proteins of the primary cilium or the centrosome. OFD1, the X-linked dominant form, is caused by mutation in the OFD1 gene. Most other forms are autosomal recessive.

checks.explanation: The abstract supports the ciliary-protein link but does not mention centrosomal proteins or say 'most numbered subtypes'.
